note: Superseding an earlier nomination of https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/nsc/ and https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/nsc/. Both ARE readable .gov pages and both DO label 'National Security Council | The White House' -- probed, they would confirm. They are refused anyway: they are NARA's frozen archives of past administrations' sites, and a confirmation from one publishes verificationMethod name_labelled_on_own_official_page with lastVerified set to the day of the fetch, which reads as 'the NSC's own official page names it, checked today'. The page has not changed since the administration ended. This project already says an archive's date in every sentence it derives from one (the PLUM archive), and a candidate page carries no such qualifier. No CURRENT page is reachable: www.whitehouse.gov/nsc/ is 404, and www.whitehouse.gov and /administration/ serve a JavaScript shell of 15 and 24 readable characters, far below the verifier's 400-character floor, so it would record nothing from them either. If an archived page is ever the right kind of evidence here, that is a deliberate policy change with its own method string, not something to slip in as an ordinary own_site nomination.
